newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on late speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on late speculation.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed up 100 basis points at 19.00 percent on Tuesday due to what traders said was surplus paper and late speculation by brokers with heavy liquidity positions.

"It is not certain what happened, no one expected it to close up, quite the opposite, but it may have been because Banco de Mexico offered more paper than expected and there was a glut of it in the system," one trader said.
The central bank intervened in the secondary market by selling 1.5 billion pesos of Cetes in direct sales, compared to 450 million pesos offered in recent sessions.
The central bank also assigned six repos totalling 3.494 billion, one of which was placed overnight at 17.97 percent.

One analyst said it was possible dealers were "hiding" their cash positions in order to cushion the expected fall in primary interest rates later in the day at Banco de Mexico's weekly primary auction of government securities.
Money market traders surveyed by Reuters revealed an average forecast assignment rate of 18.56 percentfor bellwether 28-day Cetes. This would be a drop of 115 basis points since last week.
Dealers said overnight Cetes had traded close to 17 percent for most of the session.
"In theory, overnight rates should have fallen, but the opposite happened...possibly because it is auction day and they exerrted some pressure to stop rates falling so much," a trader said.
Overnight rates on bank paper moved in parallel with government paper and ended up 45 basis points at 19.65 percent.
Liquidity of 294 million pesos was slated to return to the system on Wednesday from prior central bank participation.
